result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both pages use a centered single column of system serif body text with clear hierarchy, and each section heading has more space above than below. B's body text is slightly larger and its line spacing a little more open, at about 70 characters per line, which makes it a bit more comfortable for a long read. A's pull quote wraps awkwardly in a narrow box, and its body text is a little denser, though still good. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both pages are single-column with a constrained measure, about 19px serif body text, open leading and section headings that sit closer to the text after them. A has a slightly better line length (about 65 characters against B's 75 to 80) and roomier line spacing, and its pull quote sits cleanly on one line. B's pull quote wraps awkwardly in a box narrower than the text column. B's cream background is arguably gentler for long reading, but the rubric doesn't score colour, so A edges ahead. Both screenshots show only the top of the page, so the scores cover what is visible.
